title: Three Winters and One Short Rope
subtitle: 动物世界 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 动物世界（人与自然·自然生态·动物世界）
meta: 主题语境：动物世界（人与自然·自然生态·动物世界）　|　核心词汇：mouse　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 mouse 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1981 the herder ① caught the mouse that no neighbour in the pasture would have counted, and he said the catching was the whole of the winter. The ② mouse, meaning the rodent itself and not the rope, ran three winters and stayed uncounted in the book; a mouse, he said, is the only thing in a pasture that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ mouse in that pasture had the same short rope beside it, and the ④ mouse at the far pen, meaning the lamb they kept for the children to raise and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A mouse, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the herder said the counting is the part that fills three winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the mouse was the whole of the matter, meaning the pest and not the rodent. The ⑥ mouse, meaning the pest and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; mouse, he said, is either something you catch or the only word that means both a rodent and a pest. He said the pest is the part they remember.

By 1986 the ⑦ mouse had become a line in a ledger, and the ledger had become an argument about the short rope. The ⑧ mouse of the whole thing, the herder wrote in December, was one pasture and three winters of counting; mouse, he said, is either the lamb at the far pen or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ mouse I remember is the rodent counted in the ledger, which closed in 1988 and is still counted as the quietest in the pasture. A ⑩ mouse, my mother said in 1990, is the only rodent that improves by being counted; every mouse, she said, is a pest that has agreed to look like a rodent. She said the pest was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 老鼠；鼠标（指牧场里每一只旁边的那一只）
B. n. 老鼠；鼠标（指那只老鼠本身，与短短的缰绳相对）
C. 固定搭配：catch the mouse 捉这一只老鼠
D. n. 老鼠；鼠标（指留给孩子们养的那一只）
E. n. 老鼠之事（抽象总称，指一处牧场的老鼠之事）
F. n. 老鼠；鼠标（指牧群台账里写到、被清点的那一只）
G. n. 老鼠、祸患（指一件事里人人都养却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 祸患（抽象总称，指人人都养却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: caught the mouse that no neighbour in the pasture would have counted
The mouse, meaning the rodent itself and not the rope
the mouse at the far pen
the mouse was the whole of the matter
the mouse had become a line in a ledger
The mouse of the whole thing
A mouse, my mother said in 1990

answers.why: catch the mouse 意为“捉这一只老鼠”，1981 年那位牧人把牧场里没有一位邻人肯清点的一只老鼠做了一遍。
mouse 意为“老鼠；鼠标”，指那只老鼠本身而不是短短的缰绳，它经过了三个冬天而在簿子上没有被清点。
mouse 意为“老鼠；鼠标”，指牧场里每一只旁边的那一只，每一只旁边都有同一根短短的缰绳。
mouse 意为“老鼠；鼠标”，指最远那处圈栏的留给孩子们养的那一只，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
mouse 意为“老鼠、祸患”，指一件事里人人都养却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这只祸患就是那件事的全部。
mouse 意为“祸患”，指人人都养却无人提起的那样东西而不是那只老鼠，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
mouse 意为“老鼠；鼠标”，指牧群台账里写到、被清点的那一只，到 1986 年这一只成了牧群台账里的一行。
mouse 意为“老鼠之事”，牧人十二月写道，整件事的老鼠之事是一处牧场和三个冬天的清点。
mouse 意为“老鼠；鼠标”，我记得的是牧群台账里清点过的那一只，1988 年清点了，至今仍被说成牧场里最安静的一只。
mouse 为抽象总称，母亲 1990 年说，老鼠是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的老鼠。
